top_signals.title: Oil Prices Squeezed Between Peace Hopes and Iran Escalation Risk
top_signals.summary: Oil prices have crashed about 20% from the late-October peak of $118 per barrel, weighed down by hopes of sustainable de-escalation in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war. For months, traders and hedge funds have often bet on a resolution of the conflicts, only to reactivate buying when talks fall apart. As U.S.-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia are underway, there are no signs of a breakthrough in either the conflict in Europe or the U.S.-Iran standoff, despite messaging via Qatar. top_signals.title: Argentina Could Overtake Chile as South America’s Top Lithium Producer by 2035
top_signals.summary: Argentina could become a bigger lithium producer than Chile, mining 481,000 tons of lithium carbonate equivalent in 2035 versus 426,000 tons for Chile, GEM Mining Consulting has forecast. The shift at the top will be driven by growing demand for the battery metal. Argentina is currently the world’s fourth-largest lithium producer, after Australia, China, and Chile. alerts.title: Hybrid sales rise while battery electric sales remain lower after tax credit expiration
alerts.summary: In the third quarter of 2026 (3Q26), 23% of new light-duty vehicles sold in the United States were hybrid electric, battery electric, or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, down slightly from 24% in 3Q25. Between 3Q25 and 3Q26, hybrid electric vehicles continued to gain market share, reaching 16% of light-duty vehicle sales. Growth of hybrid electric vehicle sales has slowed this quarter as the average transaction price for a new vehicle passed $50,000-the first time this price has been reached so far this year, according to Kelley Blue Book.
